summary: Genuinely mutual NDA between Halyard and a German counterparty that largely tracks the playbook preferred positions, with only a breach-notification obligation falling outside the playbook.

findings.quote: each Party, acting as the Receiving Party, hereby covenants, undertakes and agrees with the other Party, acting as the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Obligations and the definitions of Disclosing Party and Receiving Party apply to either Party, so the NDA is truly mutual.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") or to its Representatives, whether disclosed before, on or after the Effective Date, in connection with the Purpose.
findings.why: Covers all information disclosed in connection with the Purpose by either Party, not limited to marked material, and includes derived notes and analyses in paragraph (d).

findings.quote: use the Confidential Information exclusively for the furtherance of the Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever
findings.why: Use is limited to the Purpose, which is the discussions on a potential commercial transaction and collaboration between the Parties.

findings.quote: which the Receiving Party can conclusively demonstrate by contemporaneous written records, documentary evidence or other competent proof
findings.why: All four carve-outs (3.1.1 to 3.1.4) are present with the same substance, and the evidence standard is written records or other competent proof, not tied to named personnel.

findings.quote: those Representatives and Affiliates who have a demonstrable, strict operational need to know such information
findings.why: Disclosure is allowed on a need-to-know basis to directors, officers, employees, advisers, auditors and Affiliates (Group), and the Receiving Party is liable for them under 2.1.5.

findings.quote: the Receiving Party shall, subject to applicable legal restrictions:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted by law, regulator, court or stock exchange rule, notice is qualified by legal restrictions (and 4.2), and the Receiving Party need only use reasonable commercial efforts to obtain confidential treatment, not resist at its own cost.
findings.fallback_cited: Obligation to use reasonable endeavours to obtain confidential treatment, at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten (10) Business Days following receipt of such request or upon such termination or expiration
findings.why: Return or destroy within 10 Business Days, officer certification under 5.2, and retention of automated backups and an archival copy under 5.3, which stay confidential under 5.4.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as granting, conferring, assigning or transferring, whether expressly, by implication, estoppel or otherwise, any right, title, interest, licence or intellectual property right
findings.why: No assignment, licence or ownership of improvements or feedback passes; IP stays with the Disclosing Party.

findings.quote: provided by the Disclosing Party on an "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE" basis, without any representation, warranty or guarantee of any kind
findings.why: Mutual as-is and no-warranty disclaimers with no obligation to proceed (6.4); there is no liability exclusion from which a fraud carve-out could be missing.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: not intended to involve the transfer, sharing or processing of any personal data
findings.why: Limits personal data to business contact details and requires a separate data processing or sharing agreement under 7.3 before sharing anything more.

findings.quote: fixed period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Agreement term is 3 years, within the 1 to 3 year range, with a 30-day early termination right.

findings.quote: survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years
findings.why: Survival is 5 years, within the 2 to 5 year range, and Trade Secrets are protected for as long as they remain Trade Secrets.

findings.quote: the Disclosing Party shall be entitled, without the necessity of posting any bond or other security, and without proving actual damages, to seek and obtain immediate injunctive relief
findings.why: Equitable relief is available to either Party as Disclosing Party and remedies are cumulative under 9.3; the wording is strong but mutual and there are no liquidated damages.
findings.fallback_cited: Strongly worded but mutual equitable relief.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer, novate, charge, encumber, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner
findings.why: No assignment by either Party without the other's prior written consent.

findings.quote: shall not, and shall ensure that its Representatives and Affiliates do not, reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, decrypt
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited for both Parties, save where mandatory law forbids the restriction.

findings.quote: shall be governed by, construed, interpreted and enforced in accordance with the substantive laws of England and Wales
findings.why: English law governs and clause 10.11 gives the courts of England and Wales exclusive jurisdiction.

findings.quote: shall immediately notify the Disclosing Party in writing upon becoming aware of any actual, suspected or threatened unauthorised access, acquisition, use, copying, disclosure or misappropriation
findings.why: A mutual obligation to notify immediately of suspected breaches and to cooperate in investigation and remedy is not covered by any playbook rule, so a lawyer should review it.
